question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the Directive Principles of State Policies?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 36 to 51**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are enshrined in **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution and encompass Articles **36 to 51**.
 
• They serve as guidelines to the central and state governments of India to frame laws and policies aimed at establishing a just society.
 
• **Article 36** defines the term "State" for the purposes of Part IV, the same as it is defined in Article 12 under Part III (Fundamental Rights).
 
• **Article 37** clarifies that the Directive Principles are fundamental in the governance of the country, but they are **not enforceable by any court**. However, it is the duty of the State to apply these principles while making laws.
 
• The Directive Principles are broadly classified into three categories: **Socialistic principles** (e.g., Article 38), **Gandhian principles** (e.g., Article 40), and **Liberal-intellectual principles** (e.g., Article 50).
 
• The aim of these principles is to ensure **socio-economic justice** and to establish India as a welfare state.
